slides.title: Project Overview
points: Builds a proof of concept to infer customer journeys from process diagrams in PDF files.
Converts visual workflow diagrams into structured workflow JSON for downstream orchestration use.
Targets data scientists and platform teams evaluating scalable process understanding automation.
Combines diagram extraction, flow interpretation, metadata generation, and normalized output packaging.
Uses AWS Bedrock Claude models to blend vision analysis and deterministic text transformation.
Improves repeatability versus manual diagram reading and ad hoc flow reconstruction.

slides.title: Business Problem
points: Process diagrams are often trapped in PDFs and hard to convert into machine-usable workflow structures.
Manual interpretation is slow, inconsistent, and sensitive to analyst assumptions.
Decision branches, edge labels, and loopbacks are frequently missed during hand extraction.
Static tooling struggles with mixed shapes, swimlanes, and image quality variation.
Teams need reliable conversion to journey-ready JSON for analysis and orchestration experiments.
Research required balancing classical libraries with AI-driven extraction quality.

slides.title: Solution Overview
points: Implements a three-stage pipeline optimized for workflow understanding and cost control.
Stage 1 performs vision-based node and arrow extraction with strict anti-hallucination constraints.
Stage 2 translates extracted structure into executable Mermaid flowchart syntax.
Stage 3 derives business workflow name and description from Stage 1 output.
Parser converts Mermaid nodes and connections into orchestrator-compatible JSON objects.
Validation filters non-workflow pages before expensive model execution.

slides.title: Detailed Step-Wise Execution Flow
points: Step 1: Load input PDF and rasterize pages into high-resolution workflow images.
Step 2: Validate candidate pages using edge density and directional pattern heuristics.
Step 3: Enhance accepted images for readability while preserving structural fidelity.
Step 4: Run vision model to extract node types, arrows, labels, and backward links.
Step 5: Convert structured text into Mermaid with explicit connection rules.
Step 6: Parse Mermaid into tasks, decisions, branches, and final workflow JSON files.

slides.title: Core Capabilities & Architecture
points: Supports extraction of workflow images from PDFs as reusable preprocessing capability.
Evaluates AI-driven inference quality using measurable outputs and scenario comparison.
Creates benchmarkable datasets and token-cost traces for objective experimentation.
Captures edge labels and decision branches for richer control-flow semantics.
Maintains modular architecture: conversion, extraction, parsing, cost analysis, and orchestration.
Produces standardized JSON artifacts suitable for customer journey interpretation workflows.

slides.title: Advantages
points: Reduces manual effort and accelerates workflow understanding from legacy process diagrams.
Improves extraction consistency through staged prompts and parser-backed transformation.
Balances quality and cost via hybrid model strategy across pipeline stages.
Preserves decision semantics using branch-aware JSON conversion logic.
Enables rapid experimentation across multiple diagrams with repeatable output structure.
Provides clear observability with token accounting and stage-level diagnostics.

slides.title: Limitations
points: Performance depends on diagram clarity, scan quality, and complex layout density.
Node and arrow detection can degrade on heavily stylized or ambiguous diagrams.
Mermaid parsing assumes coherent model output and may skip uncertain connections.
Prompt-driven extraction may require tuning for domain-specific notation patterns.
Current implementation focuses on proof-of-concept reliability over production hardening.
Legacy scripts indicate competing approaches still under consolidation.

slides.title: Risks & Implementation Considerations
points: Model output variability may introduce structural drift between runs on edge-case diagrams.
Cloud dependency requires stable Bedrock access, credentials, and regional configuration.
Cost can rise with large document sets without strict page filtering and batching.
Missing or unclear arrow labels can weaken downstream branch interpretation quality.
Governance needed to validate inferred workflows before operational deployment.
Fallback strategies should cover parser failures and ambiguous topology detection.

slides.title: Roadmap & Next Steps
points: Harden extraction with broader test corpus and automated quality scoring.
Expand benchmark dataset to include varied industries and notation styles.
Refine non-AI and AI hybrid options for maintainability and runtime cost.
Package pipeline into reusable service interface for orchestration consumers.
Add human-in-the-loop review for low-confidence workflow segments.
Publish recommendation framework for scaling from POC to production.
